system_description.narrative_title: Energy-driven inflation, multipolar friction, and techno-military escalation
system_description.narrative_summary: A cascade of Middle East and proxy conflicts—most visibly Iran-linked strikes and Houthi seizures of Red Sea chokepoints—has driven a renewed oil shock that is transmitting into record diesel prices and broader inflation. That energy shock is amplifying global financial stress (sharp bond selloffs, higher yields) and forcing central banks toward tighter policy even as major powers realign through BRICS diplomacy and hedging strategies. Concurrently, the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East are accelerating the militarization of advanced technologies (drones, AI-enabled systems) and pressuring states to reshape supply chains, sanctions regimes and defence-industrial ties. Domestic politics (election swings, US policy volatility) and multilateral institutions are strained as countries weigh economic pain against security imperatives.
system_description.scope: International security dynamics (Middle East, Ukraine, East Asia), global energy supply and markets, international financial markets and monetary policy, major-power diplomacy and multilateral forums (BRICS, G7/EU), technological and defense-industrial developments (AI, drones), and cross-border trade/supply-chain responses.
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic system — the international order of states embedded in the world economy, security architecture, and transnational technological and market networks.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy supply chains and commodity markets
International financial markets and central banking
Technology and defense-industrial complex (AI, drones, advanced weapons)
Domestic politics and electoral cycles in major powers

variables.name: Iran-proxy threats to Gulf–Red Sea shipping
variables.description: Iran and its proxy Houthi forces, facing Gulf state pressure, are escalating attacks on shipping and oil infrastructure, shifting acute risk onto key maritime choke points and global energy flows.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine armed confrontation
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a protracted high-intensity conflict that is expanding use of drones and missiles, straining European security, logistics and defense burdens.

variables.name: BRICS realignment and China–India rapprochement
variables.description: China and India are recalibrating bilateral ties and pushing BRICS-led economic initiatives, shifting momentum in emerging-market coordination and creating alternatives to Western-dominated institutions.

variables.name: Central-bank tightening and bond-market repricing
variables.description: Major advanced-economy central banks and global investors are recalibrating policy and risk pricing as sticky inflation and surging yields force faster rate moves and compress monetary policy room.

variables.name: US-led tech/security competition with strategic partners
variables.description: The United States and allied partners, notably South Korea, are intensifying export controls, investment screening and industrial-security measures around semiconductors, AI and data to harden supply chains amid strategic competition.
